correction.reason: The v1 lossScale of 0.75 allowed a loss-6 expression trace to outrank both exact loss-0 traces under the declared equal-family Occam target. V2 changes only lossScale to 2.0 and separates family-level deduction from hole-level deduction.

study_scope.primary_question: Under a corrected finite target whose exact traces outrank every inexact trace, does family-level deduction plus finite-choice Qwen scoring improve exact discovery over family-level deduction alone?
study_scope.primary_endpoint: paired exploratory exact discovery for D versus QD on one provider-gated seed
study_scope.secondary_endpoint: held-out exact correctness on the unchanged bounded-square oracle
study_scope.design_disclosure: This is a corrected exploratory successor to v1, created after the v1 negative result and mathematical audit. It is not confirmatory and must not be pooled with v1.
study_scope.gpu_gate: Do not run the paired provider stage until the provider-free reference audit passes. The paid provider stage remains intentionally unrun in this change.
study_scope.failure_policy: Every planned cell remains in the analysis. Timeout, provider failure, invalid artifact, failed target-dominance audit, or non-exact training result counts as failure.

stages.description: Materialize the complete finite reference locally and audit support, exact-state count, and terminal target dominance before any provider call.
One-seed exploratory D versus QD pilot, authorized only after the provider-free reference audit passes.

arms.description: Uniform finite-catalog proposal; no Qwen and no deduction guide at either level.
Uniform finite-catalog scores with deduction mixed only into family selection; specialized holes receive no deduction/Occam mixture.
Qwen finite-choice scores with a uniform support floor and no deduction guide at either level.
Qwen finite-choice scores with deduction mixed only into family selection; specialized holes use Qwen plus the uniform support floor.
